doc.title: Warren Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 17, 2018

title: Presidents and the state of the country
summary: Smith discusses presidents he favored, especially Obama, and his cautious optimism.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: You seem to be an astute observer, and I wonder what you think of what the state of our country at this moment?

I have seen presidents from Franklin Delano Roosevelt. And each succeeding one. And Roosevelt I liked a lot. I liked John F. Kennedy a lot. And I am absolutely crazy about Barack Obama. I thought he was the closest to my heart that ever got elected. But of those three, those are the only three that I favored. I didn’t even favor Kennedy as my favorite candidate at that time. There was somebody else — Adlai Stevenson was in that race and I thought Adlai Stevenson would have been a more appropriate choice. But Obama was the first one that I — you know when I first saw him I called up my cousins in Chicago and I said, “What do you think about this guy?” And they all gave him a very good rating. And then I started watching and he never disappointed me. I mean you know there were things he was forced into that had to be done, but I understand that as a black person. I understand that as a president, you know, I’ve been a chairman or a president of a fraternity or a club or whatever. And there are things that you have to do that you may not want to do or your mind isn’t in, but you have to do that for the good of the organization of whatever it is. You know, so nobody is perfect. But the rest of these people, I have not been in their corner. I have not voted for them. And they yet were able to be presidents. I have never found a Republican that I could vote for since I’ve been of voting age. But other than that I’ve still been disappointed for the most part.

Yeah. I’m optimistic that I’ll be able to hold my breath for three more years. And then we’ll see what happens. But I’m not going to be completely despondent if another poor choice gets in. Because I’ve seen poor choices get in and I’ve lived through them you know. It just means that there are areas where things might be a little bit more difficult for me, but temporarily you know. So you know, I feel good about life.
